## PLAN ROUND 1 · publish · task first-edition

**Facts found**
- No git remote is set up, and `.claude/marathon.toml` has no `[remote] publish` (`.git/config`,
  `.claude/marathon.toml`). Merges will happen locally.
- Three of the five runbooks name internal hosts or secret paths: cert-expiry
  (`secret/platform/acme-token`), disk-full (`db-primary-01.int.example.net`), and queue-backlog
  (`jobs-01.int.example.net`). deploy-rollback and dns-failure name neither (`runbooks/`).
- Every format sits behind single sign-on, and one access group grants all three. So the audience
  is that group's members whichever format you pick (`context/publishing.md`).
- The check verifies each runbook's "Use when" line and every relative link (`scripts/check.sh`).

**Currency**
- cwd: no currency command

**Questions**

1. **What format should the first edition use: a static MkDocs site on the internal docs host, a
   single PDF on the internal file share, or a Markdown index page over the runbooks in this
   repository?**
   - **rec:** the Markdown index page. It needs no build and no host, and the existing check
     already guards its links. A site or PDF can follow once the project has a remote and CI.
   - **changes:** the Markdown index adds one index page. MkDocs adds a site config and a build.
     The PDF adds a build that renders all five runbooks into one file. Each of the three needs
     one step outside this repository: granting the access group read access to this repository,
     hosting the site, or uploading the PDF.
2. **Who should the first edition reach: on-call engineers only, or on-call engineers and the
   support team?**
   - **rec:** on-call engineers only, with support's access added to the backlog as its own goal.
   - **changes:** including support adds a redaction pass over cert-expiry, disk-full, and
     queue-backlog, plus a check rule that keeps internal hosts and secret paths out of new
     runbooks.

**reply:** "1 ok, 2 ok, 3 yes but ..."
